page: Amazon Web Services m5ad.8xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an AMD EPYC 7571 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation stands at 128 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4 GB per virtual core ratio. The instance includes 1200 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 8 Gbps, with zero GPUs present.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear contrast between single-core and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core performance sits in the lower percentiles across synthetic benchmarks such as Geekbench (731.0) and stress-ng (591.09), alongside constrained single-thread gzip compression and text processing. Conversely, parallel execution scales effectively into median performance brackets, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 22,449.63, a Geekbench multi-core rating of 6,288.0, and a compilation score of 13,606.0 with Clang. Memory bandwidth reaches 1,240.55 GB/s in cached small-block reads and 61.72 GB/s in uncached large-block operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of 1200 GB of local NVMe storage reduces external block storage overhead for applications needing fast scratch space or local caching. However, tasks bound by single-core speed or modern vector instruction extensions like AVX-512 will experience architectural bottlenecks. The instance is suited for multi-threaded applications, distributed databases, batch data processing, static web serving, and memory-intensive caching tiers like Redis.
description: Amazon Web Services m5ad.8xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based virtual server equipped with an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It delivers 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 128 GB of DDR4 memory, and a dedicated 1200 GB NVMe SSD volume, supported by an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system maintains balanced compute-to-memory density with 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. Benchmark evaluations indicate modest single-thread metrics alongside solid multi-core performance, achieving 9,445.17 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 19.58 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Due to the combination of high parallel processing capacity and fast local NVMe storage, this server fits distributed backend workloads, multi-threaded compilation, intermediate ETL processing, caching systems, and relational or NoSQL database clusters.
